title: SRE dashboards + alerting for protected (enterprise) routes
creator: Allison Grant
description:
Context
- We’re adding tier-aware overload protection (gateway rate limiting + routing admission control + runtime backpressure/shed). This ticket covers the SRE-facing dashboards and paging strategy for “protected routes” (enterprise hot routes) so on-call can (a) verify enterprise SLO stability during fleet pressure and (b) triage overload events without paging storms from expected best-effort shedding.
- Motivating incident: 2025-11-03 Sev1 fleetwide latency cascade from a single hot route/noisy neighbor.

Goals
1) Provide a single Grafana landing dashboard for protected routes with per-route and per-tier breakdowns (enterprise vs best-effort), annotated with overload-protection activations.
2) Define and implement paging thresholds that align with error budgets (burn-rate based), avoid false positives during intended shedding, and are actionable.
3) Wire alerts to on-call + incident-bot with sufficient context (route, region, tier, reason, links to runbook + panels).

Non-goals
- Building new metrics in this ticket (tracked in ENG-4925/ENG-4922/ENG-4924). We can add minimal derived recording rules if needed to reduce query cost / improve alert stability.

Protected routes (MVP)
- /v1/chat/completions
- /v1/embeddings
- /v1/rerank
Notes:
- Route grouping uses “route_group” label where available (preferred) to avoid path cardinality.
- “Tier” refers to request priority class / customer tier mapping from policy engine (enterprise vs best-effort). Dedicated traffic is out of scope for MVP dashboard unless it shares the hosted gateway path.

Primary signals to visualize
- Traffic & outcomes
  - Request rate by route_group, region, tier
  - 2xx/4xx/5xx breakdown with explicit 429 reason_code breakdown
  - “shed” counters (admission control / overload shedding) by reason
- Latency
  - p50/p95/p99 end-to-end latency by route_group and tier
  - Queue depth / scheduler lag (from runtime) as leading indicator
- Capacity pressure
  - GPU saturation proxies (where reliable), queue depth, router admission decisions, scheduler lag
- Protection behavior (expected)
  - Best-effort throttled/shed earlier; enterprise remains within SLO.

Dashboard requirements (Grafana)
A) Overview (top row)
- Region selector + route_group selector
- Enterprise SLO status (SLO toolkit panel) per protected route_group
- “Protection active” indicator (last 30m) by region (derived from sustained shed_rate or admission_control_active)

B) Traffic + errors
- Requests/s by route_group x tier
- Error rate (%5xx) by route_group x tier
- 429 rate by reason_code (quota vs rate_limit vs overload_admission vs overload_shed)
- Top tenants (sampled) for debugging (must be bounded; avoid high-cardinality in default view)

C) Latency
- p95 and p99 by route_group x tier
- Tail latency heatmap by region
- Streaming termination anomalies (if available): count of aborted streams where reason=overload_shed

D) Capacity + queueing
- Runtime queue depth (aggregate) by pool/region
- Scheduler lag (aggregate) by pool/region
- Router “admission denied” counters by tier
- Batch size / utilization (aggregate) if available and low-cardinality

E) Annotations
- Overload protection activation events (from overload_event metric)
- Deploy annotations (gateway/routing/runtime) for correlation

Metric + query conventions
- Follow: Confluence observability standards “metrics-standard-overload-events-and-shed-reasons” (low-cardinality; route_group not raw path; tenant id not in default dashboards).
- Prefer recording rules for:
  - enterprise_error_rate_5m{route_group,region}
  - enterprise_latency_p99_5m{route_group,region}
  - shed_rate_5m{route_group,region,tier,reason}
  - admission_denied_rate_5m{route_group,region,tier}

Alerting plan (PagerDuty)
1) Enterprise SLO burn-rate alerts (paging)
- Use SLO toolkit (error budget burn) for each protected route_group in each region.
- Recommended multi-window burn (fast + slow) to reduce flapping:
  - Page if burn_rate_5m > 14 AND burn_rate_1h > 6 (tune per route after canary)
  - Ticket if burn_rate_30m > 3 AND burn_rate_6h > 1
- Gating to avoid paging during “expected” best-effort shedding:
  - Alerts should be computed on enterprise tier only.
  - If enterprise tier is missing label coverage, block paging until tier attribution is fixed (fallback: use allowlisted enterprise accounts only during canary).

2) Enterprise latency regression (paging)
- Page if enterprise p99 exceeds SLO threshold AND sustained queue depth / scheduler lag indicates capacity pressure.
- Proposed condition (initial):
  - enterprise_p99_latency_5m > enterprise_p99_slo_ms * 1.25
  - AND scheduler_lag_5m > lag_threshold_ms
  - for 10m
Rationale: isolate real degradations from transient spikes.

3) Overload protection misbehavior (paging)
- Page if shedding impacts enterprise tier beyond allowed budget:
  - enterprise_shed_rate_5m > 0.5% for 10m
- Page if protection is NOT activating while fleet is clearly overloaded (safety net):
  - queue_depth high + 5xx rising + admission_denied_rate(best-effort) ~0
  - (This is a “rare” alert; keep as ticket-only until we validate signal quality.)

4) Informational / ticket-only alerts
- Best-effort shed rate elevated (expected during overload): route to #incidents as FYI, no page.
- 429 reason_code distribution shifts (e.g., overload_shed increases after a config change): ticket-only + annotate dashboards.

Incident-bot integration
- Ensure alerts include:
  - route_group, region, tier
  - top panels link
  - runbook link: runbook-overload-protection-and-admission-control
  - last deploy info (if available)
- ENG-4927 is implementing incident-bot; this ticket provides field requirements + example payload.

Acceptance criteria
- Grafana dashboard exists in “SRE / Hosted API / Hot Route Protection” folder and is linked from the runbook.
- Dashboard loads in <3s with default filters (avoid expensive regex / high-cardinality queries).
- Paging alerts:
  - Trigger on canary/game day when enterprise SLO is genuinely threatened.
  - Do NOT page during expected best-effort shedding without enterprise impact.
- SLO burn-rate alerts are created via SLO toolkit repo and merged, with route_group/region scoping.

Links
- Confluence dashboard spec: sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/dashboard-spec-hot-route-protection.json
- Runbook: sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/runbook-overload-protection-and-admission-control.json
- SLO definitions: sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/hosted-api-slos-enterprise-route-tiers.json
- Postmortem: sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems/2025-11-03-sev1-fleetwide-latency-cascade-from-hot-route.json

Open questions (resolved during implementation)
- Which tier label is authoritative for “enterprise” in metrics? (Decision: use policy-derived priority_class -> tier mapping; if missing, fall back to route_group allowlist + account allowlist only for canary.)
- Do we need per-model breakdown? (Decision: keep out of default dashboard; add a drilldown dashboard with model label gated behind sampling/aggregation to avoid cardinality blowups.)

Implementation notes
- Coordinate closely with ENG-4925 to ensure queue depth + scheduler lag are aggregated per region/pool (not per replica) and exported with stable labels.
- Watch for cardinality regressions: reason_code should be a small fixed enum; route_group should be a small set; do not introduce tenant_id into base metrics.
comments: 2025-12-03 (Sergio Costa): Drafted dashboard outline based on Confluence spec + postmortem learnings. Main concern is keeping default panels low-cardinality; proposing route_group as primary dimension and a separate drilldown dashboard for tenant-level debugging (access-controlled).

2025-12-06 (Aisha Bello): For burn-rate paging, prefer multi-window (5m/1h) and page only on enterprise tier SLOs. Best-effort shedding should never page. Also +1 to adding annotations for protection activations so on-call can quickly see cause vs symptom.

2025-12-09 (Vanessa Ortiz): Capacity signals: scheduler lag and queue depth are the most reliable across regions. GPU utilization has region-specific quirks (driver/exporter variance). Please avoid paging directly on GPU util; use as context only.

2025-12-12 (Sergio Costa): Implemented initial Grafana dashboard in observability-pack branch. Added recording rules for enterprise p99 and shed_rate to reduce query load. Waiting on runtime metrics label finalization from ENG-4925 (route_group attribution).

2025-12-16 (Allison Grant): Design review: ensure 429 reason_code split is prominent. Support escalations depend on distinguishing quota vs overload_shed. Also add a panel for “enterprise denied admissions” (should be ~0) as a canary for misconfiguration.

2025-12-20 (Sergio Costa): Updated alert thresholds proposal: burn_rate paging at 14x/6x, ticket at 3x/1x. Added latency regression alert gated by scheduler lag. Sharing with Rafael for game day success criteria alignment.

2026-01-06 (Rafael Mendes): Game day ask: add a single panel that overlays enterprise p99, best-effort shed rate, and queue depth on one graph (same time axis). This was the fastest way to validate we’re protecting the right class.

2026-01-08 (Sergio Costa): Added overlay panel + annotation stream for overload-protection activations. During dry run, noticed a spike in unique label values for reason_code due to a logging-to-metric mapping bug; flagged to telemetry (Logan/Nadia).

2026-01-12 (Sergio Costa): Merged dashboards + alert rules into observability-pack. SLO burn alerts merged into slo-toolkit. Pending: final wiring to incident-bot formatting (ENG-4927) and tier attribution validation in eu-west rollout.

2026-01-21 (Sergio Costa): Post-canary tuning: reduced latency paging sensitivity (was too chatty on brief spikes). Now requires 10m sustained breach + scheduler lag gate. Verified no pages during expected best-effort shedding in us-east burst test.

2026-01-29 (Allison Grant): Marking Done. Dashboard is linked from runbook and from #eng-sre on-call topic. Follow-up: add drilldown dashboard for account-level debugging behind RBAC (new ticket to be filed if needed after GA).
